classes.class_summary: DevicesMFE is a test automation page object class that extends HPXFlow to provide verification methods for the HP Experience (HPX) Devices Micro Frontend (MFE). The class implements a comprehensive set of verification methods following a consistent naming pattern (verify_*) for validating UI elements and states in the devices management interface. Notable patterns include: (1) Extensive use of configurable timeout and exception handling parameters (raise_e) for flexible test execution, (2) Implementation of retry logic with page refresh for flaky elements (verify_supply_levels_card), (3) Support for dynamic element identification using format specifiers for printer names, (4) Verification of both element presence and invisibility states for different test scenarios, (5) Alpha code workaround for Windows dummy printer testing due to printer addition limitations, (6) Extended timeout (60 seconds) for device card loading to accommodate slow device discovery, (7) Attribute extraction capabilities for retrieving element properties like printer friendly names, and (8) Comprehensive coverage of MFE components including app bar, device status, account panel, supply levels, and navigation elements. The class demonstrates enterprise-level test automation practices with robust error handling, flexible wait strategies, and clear separation of verification concerns for different UI components.

file_summary: This Python file defines the DevicesMFE page object class for automating tests of the HP Experience Devices Micro Frontend. It contains 15 verification methods focused on validating various UI elements and states within the devices management interface, including device cards, printer information, supply levels, navigation components, and user authentication status. The implementation demonstrates advanced test automation patterns such as conditional retry logic, dynamic element identification, configurable wait strategies, and comprehensive error handling to ensure robust and maintainable test automation for the HPX devices interface.
